newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors to summon former defence minister.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors to summon former defence minister.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors will summon former defence minister Lee Yang-ho, who was sacked last week, to grill him over an arms scandal, prosecution officials said on Thursday.
"The prosecution has decided to summon Lee Yang-ho in connection with the arms scandal. He will be summoned soon, possibly later today," one official said.
President Kim Young-sam dismissed Lee on Thursday last week. Hours later the main opposition party National Congress for New Politics accused Lee of taking bribes, and Kim ordered an enquiry.

The National Congress charged that Lee and a Korean-American arms dealer split a 300 million won ($362,000) bribe from Daewoo Heavy Industries Ltd last year to arrange a government purchase of military helicopters.
Daewoo admitted giving money to the arms dealer but insisted it was a commission, not a bribe. Lee has denied accusations of wrongdoing.
Another prosecution official said three Daewoo officials were being questioned on Thursday in connection with the kickback probe.

They were Sok Chin-chol, last year's president of Daewoo Heavy, Daewoo Group chairman Yoon Young-suk and Chung Ho-shin, vice president of Daewoo Heavy, a group unit and a leading government arms contractor.
"Whether the prosecution will take further legal steps against Mr Lee will be decided after face-to-face cross questioning between him and the Daewoo officials," the prosecution official said.
Yoon, who is also chief executive officer of Daewoo Heavy, told reporters his company was deceived by the arms dealer but gave no details.
The affair has embarrassed the president who has staked his reputation on an anti-corruption crusade that has led to the trial and conviction of former presidents Roh Tae-woo and Chun Doo Hwan.
Chun was sentenced to death and Roh to 22-1/2 years in jail after being found guilty in August of corruption, mutiny and treason. Both are appealing.

The only daughter of Roh, So-young, admitted during questioning by state prosecutors earlier this week that she received diamond jewellery from the arms dealer's wife but returned it shortly afterwards after finding out that it was given to solicit a favour.

The arms dealer, Kwon Pyong-ho, told South Korean reporters in Beijing that jewels worth about $50,000 were given to try to secure Lee's promotion from lieutenant general to full general and air force chief of staff.
Lee headed the air force before becoming defence minister.
Daewoo Group founder Kim Woo-choong is currently appealing a two-year jail sentence imposed for bribing Roh. He was one of nine businessmen convicted on similar charges.
